story.headline: Reusser retains world time-trial title
story.summary: Marlen Reusser won the elite women's individual time trial at the UCI Road World Championships in Montreal, defending her title.
story.display_body: Switzerland's Marlen Reusser successfully defended her world title in the individual time trial (a solo race against the clock over a set distance — here 39.2 km through Montreal), keeping the rainbow jersey that goes to the reigning champion. She beat Britain's 21-year-old Zoe Bäckstedt by 40 seconds, with Germany's Franziska Koch third, and caught pre-race favourite Demi Vollering — who started 90 seconds ahead of her on the road — before the finish. Reusser turned 35 on the day. The road races, including the marquee elite road-race titles, run through 27 September, after this brief's window.
story.why: Reusser is one of the best against-the-clock riders of her generation, and successive world titles in an event where fractions of a second decide medals cements her as the rider to beat heading into the 2028 Olympic build-up — a rare individual world championship for Swiss sport.

story.headline: Lugano stay clear after first dropped points
story.summary: Leaders FC Lugano drew 0-0 at bottom side Lausanne-Sport, their first dropped points after eight straight wins, staying six clear atop the Swiss Super League.
story.display_body: Lugano have set the pace in Switzerland's top flight almost from kick-off, and after beating Basel 3-1 on 6 September to make it six wins from six they stretched the run to eight straight victories. That perfect start ended on Saturday: away at bottom club Lausanne-Sport they were held to a 0-0 draw — their first dropped points of the season. It barely dents the picture. Lugano sit on 25 points from nine rounds, six clear of Young Boys and Sion (both 19), with defending champions Thun down in mid-table. For a club whose modest budget and small Cornaredo stadium usually make survival the target, an unbeaten nine-game start is the story of the Swiss season so far.
story.why: The one realistic threat to Lugano is fatigue and squad depth over a long campaign; a six-point cushion this early gives them room to absorb the wobble that a 0-0 at the league's weakest side might otherwise signal.

story.headline: Atlético beat 10-man Real in Madrid derby
story.summary: Atlético Madrid beat 10-man Real Madrid 2-1 in the LaLiga derby, leaving Mourinho's side six points behind Barcelona.
story.display_body: Atlético Madrid beat their city rivals 2-1 in a bad-tempered derby that turned on a red card: Real defender Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half for hauling down Giuliano Simeone, and Alejandro Grimaldo tucked away the resulting penalty. Jonathan David added a second before Antonio Rüdiger's late header made the scoreline respectable. The result is a double blow for José Mourinho, in his first season in charge at the Bernabéu: it is Real's second league defeat already, and it leaves them six points behind leaders Barcelona and now trailing Atlético, who climb to second. Barça, unbeaten, are pulling away at the top.
story.why: A six-point gap in September is not decisive, but Real's front line — Vinícius, Mbappé and Bellingham — was kept quiet by a disciplined Atlético, and Mourinho's cautious, defensive team selection is exactly the debate his tenure was signed up to settle.

story.headline: Man City go top of the Premier League
story.summary: Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 to move three points clear at the top of the Premier League, overtaking Arsenal.
story.display_body: Manchester City won an eight-goal thriller 5-3 against Sunderland to move three points clear at the top of the English top flight, overtaking Arsenal, who had led the early table. Six games is far too soon to read much into a title race — City have stumbled at this stage before and recovered — but after a couple of uneven seasons it re-establishes them as front-runners rather than chasers.

story.headline: F1 adds a Monaco sprint for 2027
story.summary: F1 and the FIA confirmed a 24-race 2027 calendar with Sprint events expanded from six to 10, including a first-ever Monaco sprint.
story.display_body: With no race this week, the headline news came off-track: Formula 1 and the FIA published the 2027 schedule — 24 Grands Prix across 22 countries — and expanded the Sprint format (a short Saturday race that awards points, separate from the Grand Prix) from six weekends to ten. The eye-catcher is Monaco, which will stage a sprint for the first time. That is a provocative choice: the Monte Carlo street circuit is famous for being almost impossible to overtake on, so a race designed to manufacture wheel-to-wheel action is being handed the calendar's least overtaking-friendly venue. Portugal returns in June and Türkiye rejoins in October.
story.why: F1's own figures say Sprint weekends draw 12% more viewers, so the expansion is a commercial bet; whether a Monaco sprint delivers a spectacle or a procession will be the early test of whether ten sprints is one too many.

story.headline: AfD wins Mecklenburg, Left takes Berlin
story.summary: In German state elections on 20 September the AfD topped Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Die Linke won Berlin, as Merz's CDU collapsed to a record low.
story.display_body: Two German state elections on Sunday 20 September dealt Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU) their worst result on record in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and left them a distant runner-up in Berlin, where the far-left Die Linke (The Left) came first. [ongoing since 2026-09-20]. According to the Infratest dimap projections cited by Euronews, in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania the far-right AfD (Alternative for Germany) topped the poll with 38.2%, narrowly ahead of the Social Democrats (SPD) on 35.5%, while the CDU crashed to 4.9% — below the 5% threshold to enter the state parliament and its worst-ever showing there. In Berlin, Die Linke led with 25.7%, followed by the CDU on 18.8%, the AfD on 16.3%, the Greens on 14.3% and the SPD on 12.1%, a result that strips the capital's outgoing CDU–SPD coalition of its majority. Merz said there was "no way to sugar-coat" the outcome, calling the Mecklenburg result "a disaster" and conceding his party had been "squeezed out" of a contest that narrowed to a duel between the SPD and the AfD. Despite finishing first in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the AfD is unlikely to enter government there, as the other parties continue to rule out coalitions with it; SPD state premier Manuela Schwesig, who led a marked comeback, is best placed to form the next administration. These were the last state votes of the year and the figures are preliminary projections, not final certified counts.
story.why: The results are an early verdict on Merz's months-old federal government and confirm the AfD's continued rise in Germany's east, sharpening the question of how mainstream parties hold a "firewall" against a party that now wins pluralities outright.

story.headline: United Russia claims record Duma win
story.summary: United Russia won Russia's 18-20 September State Duma election with about 57.9%, a record, in a vote observers call neither free nor fair.
story.display_body: Russia's ruling United Russia party won the State Duma (the lower house of parliament) election held over three days from 18 to 20 September with about 57.9% of the vote — the highest score in its history — in a contest international observers and the brief's own reporting sources describe as neither free nor fair. [ongoing since 2026-09-18]. First results reported by SRF put United Russia on roughly 355 of the 450 seats, with the Communist Party on 13.8%, the ultranationalist LDPR on 8.8%, the New People party on 7.9% and A Just Russia on 5.1% clearing the threshold; official turnout was given as above 56%, higher than in 2021. The liberal Yabloko party was initially approved and then struck from ballots, and observers reported hundreds of monitors barred from polling stations, pre-filled ballots and people registered for online voting without their consent — a system critics call opaque and open to manipulation. For the first time the vote was staged in the Russian-occupied portions of Ukraine's Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions and in annexed Crimea, which Ukraine and most of the world reject as illegal. The count lands as Ukrainian long-range drone strikes hit Russian territory through the voting period.
story.why: A record tally engineered under tight control functions less as a genuine ballot than as a show of loyalty the Kremlin can invoke to claim popular backing for the war, and extending the vote into occupied Ukraine is a bid to normalise the annexations.

story.headline: Iran shuts French centre in Tehran
story.summary: Iran closed the French Language Center in Tehran on 20 September on a prosecutor's order; France vowed to respond ahead of a UN meeting.
story.display_body: Iran ordered the closure of the French Language Center (CLF) in Tehran on Sunday 20 September on a prosecutor's order, and France said it would respond, days before the two countries' foreign ministers are due to meet at the UN. Iran's judiciary, via its Mizan news outlet, said the centre — affiliated with the French embassy and operating "for years under the guise of language instruction" — had been shut for "illegal acts that violated diplomatic conventions," accusing it of seeking to "identify and build networks among the country's elite figures while facilitating their departure." Paris has repeatedly rejected such claims and says it has faced a pattern of intimidation as it tries to expand contact with Iranian civil society after this year's crackdown on protests. On Friday 18 September Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed a French statement as "crocodile tears" and accused Paris of historic crimes in Algeria. Araghchi and his French counterpart are still scheduled to meet on Tuesday 22 September at the annual UN General Assembly gathering in New York.
story.why: The closure is the latest turn in a bitter standoff — bound up with French nationals detained in Iran and with the wider fallout from this year's war — that now shadows a rare planned face-to-face between the two governments.

story.headline: Pakistan strikes kill three in Afghanistan
story.summary: Pakistani airstrikes on Kunar and Paktika early on 21 September killed three of one family, the Taliban said, threatening months of relative calm.
story.display_body: Pakistani airstrikes hit Afghanistan's eastern border provinces of Kunar and Paktika early on Monday 21 September, killing three members of one family and wounding four, Afghanistan's Taliban government said. Deputy government spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat said on X that a strike at around 3:00 am in Kunar's Nurgal district "completely destroyed" a house, and that two further sites — a shop and an empty house — were hit in Paktika. Pakistan had issued no public statement on the strikes at the time of reporting. The attack follows a militant assault inside Pakistan, claimed by a group linked to the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP, the "Pakistani Taliban"), that killed at least 31 people including 16 police officers. Islamabad accuses the Taliban of sheltering the TTP and Baloch separatists who mount cross-border attacks, a charge Kabul rejects as an internal Pakistani problem. The strikes threaten roughly three months of relative calm after February's cross-border clashes — the two neighbours' worst in years — which killed hundreds.
story.why: A fresh round of strikes risks reigniting open conflict between Pakistan and the Taliban government along one of South Asia's most volatile borders, with civilians bearing the immediate cost.

story.headline: VBS report clears spy service cyber unit
story.summary: A VBS administrative inquiry released 21 September found the Swiss NDB's former cyber unit sufficiently clarified, with Kaspersky questions still open.
story.display_body: The Federal Department of Defence (VBS) published on Monday 21 September the final report of an administrative investigation into the former cyber unit of the Federal Intelligence Service (NDB), concluding that the incidents there are "sufficiently clarified" and that earlier recommendations have largely been implemented, while questions over dealings with the Russian firm Kaspersky remain open. The inquiry, run by an independent law firm and commissioned in summer 2025 after an SRF investigation revealed the unit had shared sensitive data with private cybersecurity companies including Kaspersky, found no indication of large-scale data deletion or systematic espionage — no sign, in the VBS's framing, of a "Russia affair." It said "certain uncertainties" persist around the former cyber unit's cooperation with Kaspersky, which the Office of the Attorney General is still examining in a separate criminal probe. The NDB has introduced changes including new rules for reporting suspected misconduct, and a reorganisation of the cyber unit and the service is due to be completed by the end of 2026.
story.why: The report is the government's attempt to draw a line under a politically damaging affair about whether Switzerland's spy agency leaked material toward Russia — but with the prosecutor's inquiry unfinished, it stops short of fully closing the question.

story.headline: Switzerland halts Brazilian meat imports
story.summary: Switzerland has barred beef and poultry from Brazil since 3 September, following an EU ban over antibiotic-use guarantees, the BLV confirmed.
story.display_body: Switzerland has stopped importing beef and poultry from Brazil since 3 September, aligning with an EU ban imposed because Brazil could not give sufficient guarantees on antibiotic use in livestock, the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV) confirmed. EU rules bar antibiotics for growth promotion and ban so-called reserve antibiotics — those kept in reserve for human medicine — in farm animals entirely, to slow the spread of antibiotic resistance. The effect on Swiss shelves is uneven: nearly 80% of the beef eaten in Switzerland is home-produced and most imports come from Germany and Austria, so the beef impact is minimal, whereas about 40% of poultry is imported and roughly a third of that came from Brazil. The industry body Proviande calls the poultry situation manageable but does not rule out price rises.
story.why: It is a concrete, if modest, cost-of-living and food-safety story — a rule change made in Brussels and mirrored in Bern that could nudge up chicken prices and shows how closely Swiss import standards track the EU's.
